CHARTER ORDINANCE NO.
Date:
ADMINISTRATOR AND EXEMPTING THE CITY OF CHEYENNE, ASA
FIRST CLASS CITY, FROM CERTAIN SECTIONS OF THE WYOMING
STATUTES."
WHEREAS, the City of Cheyenne hasbeen established and is currently operatingas afirst
class city pursuant to the Constitution and Laws of the State of Wyoming; and
WHEREAS, Article13, Section 1, of the Wyoming Constitution provides in part that a
Wyoming city or town may elect that the whole or any part of any statute, other than statutes
uniformly applicable to all cities andtowns and statutes prescribing limits of indebtedness, shall not
apply to such city ortown; and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Article13, Section1, of the Wyoming Constitution, the Governing
Body desires to provide for the position of City Administrator and to exempt the City of Cheyenne
from certain sections of the Wyoming Statutes that relate only to first class cities and that would
restrictthe powers delegated to and duties imposed upon the City Administrator as envisioned in this
Charter Ordinance; and
WHEREAS, Article 13, Section 1.(c) of the Wyoming Constitution provides that the
Governing Body may submit, without petition, any charter ordinance to referendum election by
referendum election, and the Governing Body desires to submit to qualified municipal electors a
ballot question regarding whether this Charter Ordinance shall take effect.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY
OFCHEYENNE, WYOMING:
SECTION 1.The City of Cheyenne shall not be governed by the provisions of W.S.Ss15-3-204,
15-3-207,15-3-208, and 15-3-209 through 15-3-212.
SECTION 2. The following provisions shall apply to and govern the City of Cheyenne:
A.The Governing Body shall employa City Administrator and City Attorney, and fix
their salaries.The City Administrators hall receive no other or additional salary for the performance
of any ofthe duties required as City Administrator.The City Administrator and City Attorney are
employees of and serve at the pleasure of the Governing Body.The salaries of the City
Administrator and City Attorney may be changed from year to year.The City Administrator and
City Attorney may be discharged and their employment terminated at any time by a majority vote
of the qualified members of the Governing Body.
1:
B.If the City Administrator position becomes vacant for any reason, the Governing Body
shall immediately proceed to employ another person.If there is a delay in appointing a new City
Administrator, the Governing Body shall designate and fix the salary of an acting City Administrator.
In the event the Mayor is designated as acting City Administrator, the Mayor shall receive no
compensation other thanthat provided for the office of Mayor.The acting City Administrators hall
until a City Administrator is hired and qualified.
C.The City Administrator shall appoint, and the Governing Body shall confirm, two (2)
or more municipal judges to hear and determine all cases arising under the ordinances of the City
of Cheyenne that are within the jurisdiction of the Municipal Court.The municipal judges shall serve
at the pleasure of the City Administrator.
D.Except for the City Administrator and City Attorney, and except as provided in
Sub-SectionG., of this Section, all employees shall be employed by the City Administrator, selected
onmerit and serve at the pleasure of the City Administrator, subject to applicable personnel rules
and regulations and applicable law.The City Administrator shallfix employee salaries, by andwith
the consent of the Governing Body, consistent with the City's ability to pay.Nothing herein shall
be construed as affecting or superseding the provisions ofW.S.Ss15-5-101 through15-5-422 or
W.S.Ss27-10-101 through 27-10-109.
E.Subject to confirmation by the Governing Body, the Mayor shall, in the manner
provided by state law, appoint themembers of the City of Cheyenne Board of Public Utilities, the
Planning Commission, the Board of Adjustment, the City Police Department Civil Service
Commission, and the City Fire Department Civil Service Commission.Subject to confirmation by
the Governing Body, if required by ordinances amended pursuant to Section 3 of this Charter
Ordinance, the City Administrator shall appoint the members of all other City boards, committees,
and commissions that are not otherwise subject to specific appointment procedures provided by state
law.Subject to confirmation by the Governing Body, if required by ordinances amended pursuant
to Section 3 of this Charter Ordinance, by-laws, or other organizational documents, the City
Administrator shall appoint the members of joint powers boards and other inter-governmental
boards, commissions, and committees.
F.In addition to the specific duties set forth in this Charter Ordinance, the City
Administrator shall see that all laws and ordinances are observed and enforced.The City
Administrator shall prepare and submit to the Governing Body reports required by it, and others as
deemed advisable.The City Administrators hall keepthe Governing Body fully advised ofthe City's
administration after its approval. The City Administrator shall perform all duties imposed by the
ordinances of the City that are not inconsistent with state law.The City Administrator is the
purchasing agent for the city.

G.The City Administrator shall appoint, subject to confirmation by the Governing Body,
the City Clerk, City Engineer, City Treasurer, Parks and Recreation Director, Planning Services
Director, Development Director, Public Works Director, Police Chief, and Fire Chief.Subject to
applicable law and personnel rules and regulations, the City Administrator mayhire and remove
subordinates, clerks, assistants, employees and laborers and fix the compensation of those appointed
within the limits fixed by the Governing Body and thelaw.Except as otherwise provided, the City
Administrators hall prescribe the powers and duties of all employees, and may require anyemployee
to perform duties in two(2)ormore departments.The City Administrator shall file with the Human
Resources Director and City Treasurer a listofthe names of all employees, together with a statement
of the salary or compensation eachis to receive.The City Administrator shall recommend to the
Governing Body such rules and regulations as necessary for the efficient and economical conduct
of the business of the City.
H.The City Treasurer shall perform those duties and functions and be subject to those
restrictions and limitations specified in the “Uniform Municipal Fiscal Procedures Act”, W.S.$
16-4-101, et seq., and other applicable provisions of law. The City Treasurer shall post a bond
pursuant tow.S.15-1-124.
1.The Governing Body may employ experts to perform unusual or special services upon
the recommendation of the Administrator or otherwise.
SECTION 3. All ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict herewith shall be amended pursuant
to separate ordinances approvedby the Governing Body in conjunction with and to become effective
on the same date as the effective date of this Charter Ordinance.
SECTION4.If any section, clause or phase shall be held unconstitutional or invalid, it shall not
affect the balance of this ordinance, which shall remain in full force andeffect.
SECTION 5.Pursuant to Article 13, Section 1.(c) of the Wyoming Constitution, the Governing
Body of the Cityof Cheyenne hereby proclaims that a special referendum election on this Charter
Ordinances hall be conducted on Tuesday November10,2015.Election procedures shall be set forth
in a separate ordinance to be approved by the Governing Body in compliance with Article 13,
Section 1.(c) of the Wyoming Constitution, and any applicable special municipal election laws.
After approval of this Charter Ordinance by the Governing Body, the City Clerkshall providefor
the publication of this Charter Ordinance in a newspaper of general circulation in the City of
Cheyenne once each week for two (2) consecutive weeks.The Mayor and City Clerk are herewith
directed to comply with the provisions of state law relating to a special municipal referendum
election and are authorized to request and receive the assistance of the County Clerk of Laramie
County, Wyoming, in preparing, proclaiming, and conducting said special municipal referendum
election.

SECTION 6.This Charter Ordinance shall be effective upon approval by the Governing Body, upon
publication of the same in the manner provided by law and upon the approval of this Charter
Ordinance by a majority of the qualified municipal electors voting thereon at the special referendum
election to be conducted on Tuesday, November 10, 2015, provided however, that this Charter
Ordinance shall become effective not sooner than January3,2017.
